summary: Checks whether a value is **not** an object.
description: `nonObject(value)` is the same test as `!isObject(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
The test is `typeof value === "object"` with `null` excluded, so arrays, dates and class instances all count, while a function does not. `isObjectLike` is the one that also accepts functions.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not an object; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonObject(null); // => true
nonObject("abc"); // => true
nonObject(function () {}); // => true
nonObject({}); // => false
nonObject([]); // => false
nonObject(new Date()); // => false
```
